forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. The 45-day ceasefire extension announced by the US State Department on 15 May remained formally in place as of EOD 22 May 2026. No US or Lebanese government statement declared the ceasefire void or withdrawn. IDF conducted daily strikes in southern Lebanon within the ceasefire's carve-out provision; no strikes in Beirut's governorate were recorded. Hezbollah did not exceed the 50/day rocket threshold. Both indicators NOT_OBSERVED. Resolution criteria for YES not met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: On 20 May 2026, the Knesset passed a coalition-backed dissolution bill in preliminary reading by a vote of 110-0, with no lawmakers voting against. A parallel opposition bill sponsored by Benny Gantz passed preliminary reading 53-0. Degel HaTorah spiritual leader Rabbi Dov Lando publicly instructed lawmakers to support dissolution. Netanyahu attempted on 20 May to reintroduce the haredi draft-exemption bill in the Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee as a retention mechanism; the attempt was rejected by ultra-Orthodox members. Neither bill specifies an election date; Israeli procedure requires three further readings before a bill has force of law. Netanyahu has made no formal announcement of an election date as of 22 May. Probability raised from 0.22 to 0.38: the 110-0 preliminary vote reflects genuine collapse of coalition discipline, but formal resolution of the June-1 criterion (a named date announcement or completed dissolution vote) within 10 days remains narrow under standard Israeli legislative timelines. Cross-reference: if NF1 (id=2026-05-22-knesset-dissolution-bill-final-passage-by-june-10) resolves YES before EOD 2026-06-01, this forecast also resolves YES simultaneously.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. Cross-reference: if NF1 (id=2026-05-22-knesset-dissolution-bill-final-passage-by-june-10) resolves YES before EOD 2026-06-01, this forecast also resolves YES simultaneously.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran FM Baghaei confirmed on 21 May that Tehran was 'reviewing' the latest US text. Iran's semi-official ISNA described the proposal as having 'narrowed the gaps to some extent' — the most constructive public signal from an Iranian-linked outlet since negotiations began, and a plausible authorized trial balloon given ISNA's proximity to pragmatist government circles. Bloomberg confirmed two hard stops remain: Supreme Leader Khamenei issued a directive that uranium stockpiles must not leave Iranian territory (US demands physical transfer), and Iran's Hormuz toll demand is unresolved. Pakistan's Interior Minister Naqvi arrived in Tehran 21-22 May as special envoy; Army Chief Munir postponed his own visit pending a 'final formula.' No direct Witkoff-Araghchi meeting confirmed. Rubio noted 'good signs' but kept 'other options' available. ISNA's constructive framing warrants holding above 0.20; the Khamenei uranium directive — a constraint from the system's terminal authority — argues against maintaining at 0.25. Probability revised from 0.25 to 0.22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; direct principal-level engagement removed Pakistani-channel lag in April.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; Trump's typical pre-announcement framing on social media has been a leading indicator.

forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: IMF PortWatch recorded 2 independent commercial transits on 21 May — 2% of the pre-crisis baseline of ~95-120/day. Lloyd's war-risk premiums at ~8× pre-crisis; 6 P&I clubs have withdrawn Hormuz cover entirely. Maersk and MSC have not announced returns. Polymarket's 'Hormuz normal by end of May' market traded at 5%. Iranian Navy claimed 31 transits on 22 May, but that count includes IRGC-escorted tankers excluded under the forecast's ambiguity rule. Brent at ~$116.73 on 21 May. The only path to YES by June 10 runs through a signed Iran-US framework deal producing simultaneous insurance re-entry; as of 22 May that deal has not materialized. Structured estimate: P(YES|deal) × P(deal) + P(YES|no deal) × P(no deal) ≈ 0.40 × 0.22 + 0.03 × 0.78 ≈ 0.112; Judge rounds to 0.12. Probability revised from 0.38 to 0.12.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA addendum: third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

forecasts.question: Will the Israeli Knesset dissolution bill (or equivalent dissolution instrument) pass third and final reading in Knesset plenary before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The dissolution bill passed preliminary reading 110-0 on 20 May 2026, with support across coalition and opposition including Degel HaTorah, Shas, Religious Zionist Party, and Gantz's bloc. Three additional readings plus committee review are required before the bill has force of law. Netanyahu's internal opposition to September elections is noted but he lacks votes to obstruct the process. Standard Israeli legislative timelines give the June-10 window a moderate-to-high probability for final passage, conditional on no coalition-breaking deal (e.g. haredi draft-exemption compromise) materializing within 19 days. p=0.55. Cross-reference: if this forecast resolves YES before EOD 2026-06-01, F2 (id=2026-05-19-netanyahu-early-election-by-june-1) also resolves YES simultaneously.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a dissolution bill passes third and final reading in Knesset plenary per official Knesset vote record; OR if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech naming an early election date. NO if no such vote or announcement occurs before EOD 2026-06-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Official Knesset vote record + at least two of: Times of Israel, Haaretz, Channel 12/13, Jerusalem Post. Reuters/AP confirmation for international sourcing.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Second reading without third = NOT resolved YES. Knesset committee approval alone without plenary third reading = NOT resolved YES. If the bill passes but Netanyahu challenges it legally and the Supreme Court enjoins enforcement: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Cross-reference: if this forecast resolves YES before EOD 2026-06-01, F2 (id=2026-05-19-netanyahu-early-election-by-june-1) also resolves YES simultaneously.
